summary: Two-panel toolbar control for choosing one grouping data point and the order of its group sections.
useWhen: A data view needs explicit control of one grouping level and its section order.
Grouping data-point labels differ from compact table-header labels.
avoidWhen: The data view is not groupable.
The application expects the component to rearrange rows or create group sections internally.

alternatives.when: The choice is one submitted form value with no dependent order pane.
alternatives.reason: Select owns form-value semantics rather than table grouping state.

accessibility: The trigger opens a named non-modal dialog. Data and Order are independently named single-selection listboxes.
Up and Down move within the focused pane. Right moves from Data to Order when a group is active, Left returns to the selected Data row, and Escape closes the dialog and restores trigger focus.
The right pane remains present before a group is active as one complete empty state without the Order heading, and explains that a group must be selected.
states: options and grouping are controlled. A data option may supply product-owned orderOptions; otherwise Order defaults to Ascending and Descending. dsGroupChange reports a complete DataGroupingState and dsClear requests null grouping without mutating either input.
Selecting a new data point starts at its first custom order option, or ascending when it has no custom order options. Re-selecting the active data point preserves its complete order state.
Selecting a data point or direction applies immediately and leaves the dialog open so the other pane can be changed.
The grouping picker automatically holds the shared surface-open wash through exit. Opening this picker is separate from expanding an inline table group.
Embedded mode renders the same controlled content inside a parent-owned surface; the parent owns positioning, initial focus, Escape, Tab exit, and dismissal.
Borderless toolbar compositions omit resting control borders while retaining focus and interaction feedback.
Expanded toolbar triggers use an icon and regular-weight text without a trailing chevron.
Vertical presentation stacks grouping data and ordering, with an explicit No grouping choice and no Clear footer.
responsiveBehavior: Use in the trailing region of ds-data-toolbar.
The trigger uses the shared caption-control button behavior and becomes icon-only in compact table captions or standalone data toolbars.
Both panes remain present and their choice lists scroll within the collision-constrained popup.

customElements: Assign options and grouping as JavaScript properties and replace grouping from dsGroupChange or dsClear.
react: Keep grouping in application state and replace it from dsGroupChange; set it to null from dsClear.
angular: Import the generated DsDataGroup adapter and bind options and grouping as properties.

styling.rationale: The component owns the protected recipes below; unspecified host properties and application layout remain customizable.

protected.reason: The component owns its surface and interaction treatment; use its semantic presentation props or compose an application-owned surrounding surface.
The component owns its surface radius; retain the shared recipe and customize an outer wrapper when needed.
